title: Neither Minimum nor Maximum
statement:
The array `nums` holds distinct positive integers. Return one of its values that is strictly greater than the array's smallest value and strictly less than its largest value. If `nums` has no such value, return `-1`.

When several values qualify, any one of them is accepted.
constraints: The values in nums are pairwise distinct
notes:
## Intuition

The obvious way is to find the minimum and maximum in one pass and then return any other value. There is a shortcut: take any three distinct values. The middle one has a smaller value beside it and a larger value beside it, so it cannot be the array's minimum or its maximum. So only the first three entries matter, and sorting just those three gives the answer in constant time.

With fewer than three values, every value is the minimum or the maximum, so the answer is `-1`.

## Approach

1. If `nums` has fewer than 3 values, return `-1`.
2. Copy the first three values into `firstThree`.
3. Sort `firstThree` numerically.
4. Return its middle element, `firstThree[1]`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [3, 2, 1, 4]` has four values, so an answer exists. `firstThree = [3, 2, 1]`, which sorts to `[1, 2, 3]`. The `middle` is `2`: `1` is smaller and `3` is larger, so `2` is neither the minimum (1) nor the maximum (4). Return `2`. (`3` would also be accepted.)

## Complexity

- Time: O(1): only three values are sorted, whatever the array's length.
- Space: O(1) for the three-element copy.

## Pitfalls

- JavaScript's default `sort` compares as strings (`[100, 20, 3]` stays in that order); pass `(a, b) => a - b`.
- Check the length first: with one or two values, `nums[2]` is `undefined`.
- Sorting the whole array also works but costs O(n log n) for no benefit.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `firstThree` | copy of the first three values of `nums`, sorted |
| `middle` | the middle of those three, never the array's minimum or maximum |

narration.2: With fewer than three distinct values, each one is the minimum or the maximum.
narration.3: So no value qualifies and the answer is -1.
narration.5: Take any three values; the first three are the easiest to reach.
narration.6: Sort them numerically so the middle one sits at index 1.
narration.7: The middle has a smaller and a larger value beside it, so it is neither the minimum nor the maximum of nums.
